title: JavaScript syntax basics: names, operators, control flow, and template literals
intro: This module teaches the building blocks of JavaScript syntax: how to name variables, write expressions, make decisions, repeat work, and format strings. Every topic uses plain English, runnable code, and comparisons with C# and TypeScript so nothing feels mysterious.

conceptCards.title: Identifiers, keywords, and literals
conceptCards.summary: Names you choose, words the language reserves, and values you write directly. JavaScript has Automatic Semicolon Insertion (ASI) — unlike C#.
conceptCards.example: const count = 199; const json = `{"ok":true}`; // backtick multi-line

conceptCards.title: var, let, const, and TDZ
conceptCards.summary: Block-scoped let/const with temporal dead zone. var is function-scoped and hoisted to undefined — legacy only.
conceptCards.example: const config = { retries: 3 }; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { /* closure-safe */ }

conceptCards.title: Operators and precedence
conceptCards.summary: === strict equality, ?? nullish coalescing, ?. optional chaining. Precedence traps when mixing ?? with || or ?:.

conceptCards.title: if, switch, and truthiness
conceptCards.summary: if accepts truthy/falsy — not bool-only like C#. switch uses ===. Eight falsy values to memorize.

conceptCards.title: for, while, for-of, for-in
conceptCards.summary: for-of walks iterable values (like C# foreach). for-in enumerates object keys — avoid on arrays.

conceptCards.title: break, continue, return, labels
conceptCards.summary: Jump statements transfer control. Labels break outer nested loops. break/continue do not work inside forEach.
conceptCards.example: if (bad) continue; return null; outer: for (...) { break outer; }

conceptCards.title: Template literals and tags
conceptCards.summary: Backticks for multi-line strings and ${interpolation}. Tagged templates call a function with string parts and values.
